Do the three levels join up as one continuous run, or does the player load into each one separately?

captured: neon cyberpunk highway with moving grid walls, laser beams and booster pads
futuristic factory with rotating electric rollers, timed laser gates and toxic waste pits
crumbling space station with vanishing platforms and swinging pendulums
spinning gold coins across all levels
glowing green checkpoint pads at each section start
contact with hazards resets to checkpoint

enriched_invented.detail: coins floating above the ground rather than on the platforms
wide corridors lining the factory rollers
a forward-facing camera emphasising speed

notes_for_us: Walk speed 40 is two and a half times the baseline the genre's jump limits are derived from, so the 11-stud and 7.2-stud gap ceilings in the Obby file are wrong for this build. Nothing in the skill lets a prompt restate the movement baseline that P6 validates against, and here the prompt did exactly that.
The three levels are the clearest segments case in the batch and each has its own theme, which the per-segment theme field held cleanly.
Booster pads went to powerup-buffs, which reads as a pickup rather than a surface. It fits functionally but the wording will arrive wrong.

unmatched_options.text: high-speed booster pads embedded in the ground that accelerate the player forward
set player default walk speed to 40
collected coins add +1 to a global Coins leaderboard
a UI menu button labelled Shop where players spend coins on trail effects
floating platforms that disappear 1 second after touch

skill_gap.name: movement baseline override
skill_gap.why: the genre's P6 gap limits are derived from default WalkSpeed, and a prompt that sets walk speed to 40 invalidates them with no field to carry the new baseline
